nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with $n \ge 2$ vertices, $m$ edges (counted with multiplicity) and minimum cut size $k$. Then $n k \le 2m$: every vertex has degree at least $k$, since its singleton is a cut.
nodes.title: Minimum cut size bounds the number of edges

nodes.summary: For a multigraph state $G$ and a pair of vertices $e = (a, b)$, the contraction of $G$ along $e$ deletes the first occurrence of $b$ from the vertex list, replaces $b$ by $a$ in both endpoints of every edge, and then deletes every edge whose two endpoints are equal.
nodes.title: Edge contraction

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph state, $e = (a, b)$ a pair of vertices and $Y$ a map from vertices to booleans, and let $\rho$ send $b$ to $a$ and fix every other vertex. The size of the cut $Y$ in the contraction of $G$ along $e$ equals the size of the cut $Y \circ \rho$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Cut sizes under contraction

nodes.summary: For a list of edges (pairs of vertices, repeated pairs counted with multiplicity) and a map $X$ from vertices to booleans, the size of the cut $X$ is the number of edges $(u, v)$ in the list with $X(u) \ne X(v)$.
nodes.title: Size of a cut

nodes.summary: Two maps $X, Y$ from vertices to booleans are distinct on a list of vertices $S$ when some $v \in S$ has $X(v) \ne Y(v)$ and some $w \in S$ has $X(w) = Y(w)$; so on $S$ neither cut is the other or its complement.
nodes.title: Cuts distinct as partitions

nodes.summary: A map $X$ from vertices to booleans is a cut of a multigraph state $G$ when some vertex $v$ of $G$ has $X(v) = \mathrm{true}$ and some vertex $w$ of $G$ has $X(w) = \mathrm{false}$.
nodes.title: Cuts of a multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with minimum cut size $k$, and let $X$ be a cut of $G$ of size $k$. If $e = (a, b)$ is an edge of $G$ with $X(a) = X(b)$, then the contraction of $G$ along $e$ also has minimum cut size $k$.
nodes.title: Contraction preserves the minimum cut size

nodes.summary: A natural number $k$ is the minimum cut size of a multigraph state $G$ when some cut of $G$ has size $k$ and every cut of $G$ has size at least $k$.
nodes.title: Minimum cut size

nodes.summary: For vertices $a$ and $b$, renaming $b$ to $a$ is the map on vertices that sends $b$ to $a$ and fixes every other vertex.
nodes.title: Renaming a vertex

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph state with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $t$ be a natural number with $n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process returns $k$ is at least $1/2$.
nodes.title: Repeating Karger's algorithm succeeds with probability at least one half

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $t$ be a natural number with $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil \cdot n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at least $1 - 1/n$.
nodes.title: Karger's algorithm succeeds with high probability

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$, and let $c$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $c \cdot n(n-1) \le 2t$. Then the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs of the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at least $1 - (1/2)^c$.
nodes.title: Amplification with high probability

nodes.summary: For a multigraph $G$ with $n$ vertices and natural numbers $k$ and $t$, let $p$ be the probability that one run of the contraction process on $G$, with $n$ contractions allowed, returns $k$. The repeated success probability is $1 - (1 - p)^t$, the probability that at least one of $t$ independent runs returns $k$.
nodes.title: Success probability of repeated runs

nodes.summary: A state over a vertex type $V$ consists of a list of current (super-)vertices in $V$ and a list of edges, each an ordered pair of elements of $V$; repeated pairs are parallel edges.
nodes.title: Multigraph state of Karger's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices and minimum cut size $k$. Then the contraction process on $G$, with $n$ contractions allowed, returns $k$ with probability at least $2 / (n(n-1))$.
nodes.title: Karger's bound

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, every number of allowed contractions and every multigraph $G$, the probability that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The success probability is at most one

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, every number $f$ of allowed contractions and every multigraph state $G$, the probability $P_k(f, G)$ that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ satisfies $0 \le P_k(f, G)$.
nodes.title: The success probability is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a number $f$ of allowed contractions and a multigraph $G$ with edge list $E_G$, the probability $P_k(f, G)$ that the contraction process on $G$ returns $k$ is defined by recursion on $f$. If $f = 0$, or $G$ has at most two vertices, or $G$ has no edges, then $P_k(f, G)$ is $1$ when $G$ has exactly $k$ edges and $0$ otherwise. Otherwise…
nodes.title: Success probability of the contraction process

nodes.summary: For a valid multigraph $G$, the sum over the vertices $v$ of $G$ of the number of edges crossing the singleton cut $\{v\}$ equals twice the number of edges of $G$.
nodes.title: Handshake lemma

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with vertex list $S$, let $f$ be a number of allowed contractions, and let $X_1, \dots, X_m$ be Boolean functions on the vertex type that are pairwise distinct as partitions of $S$. Then the probabilities that the contraction process on $G$, with $f$ contractions allowed, outputs $X_1, \dots, X_m$ add up to at most $1$.
nodes.title: Survival probabilities of distinct cuts sum to at most one

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices whose minimum cut size $k$ is at least $1$, and let $X$ be a cut of $G$ with exactly $k$ crossing edges. Then the probability that the contraction process on $G$, allowed up to $n$ contractions, outputs the cut $X$ is at least $2/(n(n-1))$.
nodes.title: Each minimum cut survives with probability at least $2/(n(n-1))$

nodes.summary: For a map $X$ from vertices to booleans, a fuel bound $f$ and a multigraph $G$, this is the probability that the contraction process on $G$ (contract an edge chosen uniformly at random, counted with multiplicity, while more than two vertices and at least one edge remain, making at most $f$ contractions) never contracts an edge whose endpoints $X$ separates and ends with exactly two vertices on which $X$ takes both…
nodes.title: Probability that a run outputs a given cut

nodes.summary: At most $n(n-1)/2$ minimum cuts (Karger; Kleinberg and Tardos, Section 13.2). Let $G$ be a valid multigraph with $n \ge 2$ vertices whose minimum cut size $k$ is at least $1$. If $X_1, \dots, X_m$ are cuts of $G$, each with exactly $k$ crossing edges, that are pairwise distinct as partitions of the vertices of $G$, then $2m \le n(n-1)$, that is, $m \le n(n-1)/2$.
nodes.title: At most $n(n-1)/2$ minimum cuts

nodes.summary: If a multigraph $G$ is valid and $e$ is one of its edges, then the contraction of $G$ along $e$ is valid and has exactly one vertex fewer than $G$.
nodes.title: Contraction preserves validity and removes one vertex

nodes.summary: A multigraph, given by a list of vertices and a list of edges (pairs of vertices, with multiplicity), is valid when its vertex list has no repeated entries and every edge joins two distinct vertices of the list.
nodes.title: Valid multigraph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
